q: Environment is everything that is around us. It can be living (biotic) or non-living (______).
e: Environment is everything that is around us. It can be living (biotic) or non-living (abiotic). Abiotic factors are the non-living parts of the environment. Aquatic is not abiotic.

q: The four major components of the environment together are known as the ______.
e: The four major components of the environment together are known as the ecosphere. The ecosphere is hydrosphere, lithosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere together. The environment is classified into four major components that make the ecosphere. Biosphere is different: the biosphere is the global life layer where living things exist.

q: The hydrosphere includes all ______ such as lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, and oceans.
e: The hydrosphere includes all water bodies such as lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, and oceans. The hydrosphere is all water bodies: lakes, rivers, seas, and oceans. Gaseous layers is not water bodies.

q: Lithosphere mainly contains soil, earth rocks, mountains, etc., and is divided into three layers: crust, mantle, and ______.
e: Lithosphere mainly contains soil, earth rocks, mountains, etc., and is divided into three layers: crust, mantle, and core. The lithosphere is the rock and soil crust of the earth. Rocks and soil belong to the lithosphere. Exosphere is different: the exosphere is the outermost fringe of atmosphere, not the life layer.

q: The cover of air that envelopes the Earth is known as the ______.
e: The cover of air that envelopes the Earth is known as the atmosphere. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth. Hydrosphere is different: the hydrosphere is all water bodies: lakes, rivers, seas, and oceans.

q: The biosphere is otherwise known as the ______.
e: The biosphere is otherwise known as the life layer. The life layer is the biosphere, where living things actually exist. The biosphere is the global life layer where living things exist. Rock layer is not life layer.

q: An ecosystem is a functional unit of nature where living organisms interact among themselves and also with the surrounding ______.
e: An ecosystem is a functional unit of nature where living organisms interact among themselves and also with the surrounding physical environment. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic. Biological molecules occur naturally inside living organisms, not in bare rock. Solar radiation is not physical environment.

q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a terrestrial ecosystem in the textbook?
e: Coral reef NOT listed as a terrestrial ecosystem in the textbook? Coral reefs are highly productive marine ecosystems built by coral animals and algae. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials. Grassland is not coral reef.

q: Freshwater ecosystems comprise about ______ of the Earth's surface.
e: Freshwater ecosystems comprise about 1.8% of the Earth's surface. 71% is not 1.8%.

q: Marine ecosystems are the ______ ecosystem of the Earth.
e: Marine ecosystems are the largest ecosystem of the Earth. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials. Most polluted is not largest.

q: In an ecosystem, green plants that photosynthesise to produce food are called ______.
e: In an ecosystem, green plants that photosynthesise to produce food are called producers. Producers, mainly green plants, convert light to chemical energy. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials. Decomposers is different: decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead material and recycle nutrients.

q: Animals that eat plants or other animals are known as ______.
e: Animals that eat plants or other animals are known as consumers. Consumers get energy by eating other organisms. Reducers is not consumers.

q: Organisms that break down dead material and help to recycle nutrients are called ______.
e: Organisms that break down dead material and help to recycle nutrients are called decomposers. Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead material and recycle nutrients. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome. Herbivores is not decomposers.

q: Abiotic factors include all of the following EXCEPT ______.
e: Abiotic factors include all of the following EXCEPT predation. Predation is one biotic interaction that structures communities. Abiotic factors are the non-living parts of the environment. Temperature is not predation.

q: Biotic factors include all of the following EXCEPT ______.
e: Biotic factors include all of the following EXCEPT salinity. Biotic factors are the living parts of the environment. Competition for food is not salinity.

q: All the organisms of a particular species found in an ecosystem at a certain time form a ______.
e: All the organisms of a particular species found in an ecosystem at a certain time form a population. A population is all the individuals of one species in an area. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials. Habitat is different: a habitat is the place where an organism lives.

q: The populations of all species found in an ecosystem at a particular time form the ______.
e: The populations of all species found in an ecosystem at a particular time form the community. A community is all the populations living together in an area. An ecosystem is a community plus its physical environment, linked by energy and materials. Ecosphere is different: the ecosphere is hydrosphere, lithosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere together.

q: In a food chain, the arrow (→) means ______.
e: In a food chain, the arrow (→) means is eaten by. A food chain is one linear feeding path from producer onward. Competes with is not is eaten by.

q: The different stages in a food chain (producer, primary consumer, secondary consumer) are called ______.
e: The different stages in a food chain (producer, primary consumer, secondary consumer) are called trophic levels. Trophic levels are feeding steps in a food chain. A food chain is one linear feeding path from producer onward. Feeding zones is not trophic levels.

q: A food web shows feeding relationships with ______.
e: A food web shows feeding relationships with different food chains. Agriculture and husbandry both serve food production, but they are different practices. A food web is the network of linked food chains in a community. Only decomposers is not different food chains.

q: Pollution is the effect of ______ changes in our surroundings that have harmful effects on plants, animals and human beings.
e: Pollution is the effect of undesirable changes in our surroundings that have harmful effects on plants, animals and human beings. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment. Reversible is not undesirable.

q: A substance which causes pollution is called a ______.
e: A substance which causes pollution is called a pollutant. A pollutant is a substance that harms air, water, soil, or living things. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment. Waste is not pollutant.

q: Which of the following is NOT listed as one of the seven major types of pollution?
e: Chemical pollution NOT listed as one of the seven major types of pollution? Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment. Biochemistry looks at chemical substances and chemical processes in cells.

q: Air pollution can be caused by all of the following EXCEPT ______.
e: Air pollution can be caused by all of the following EXCEPT photosynthesis. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment. Industries is not photosynthesis.

q: Water pollution causes diseases such as dysentery, typhoid, jaundice and ______.
e: Water pollution causes diseases such as dysentery, typhoid, jaundice and fever. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment. Diabetes is not fever.

q: Land pollution leads to soil erosion, shift of animals' habitats and adverse effects on the health of ______.
e: Land pollution leads to soil erosion, shift of animals' habitats and adverse effects on the health of animals and humans. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment. Medicine and veterinary science restore and maintain health. Plants only is not animals and humans.

q: Noise pollution is caused by machines, transport, construction sites, etc., and can cause ______.
e: Noise pollution is caused by machines, transport, construction sites, etc., and can cause high blood pressure. Blood carries gases, nutrients, hormones, and wastes around the body. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment. Vitamin deficiency is not high blood pressure.

q: Thermal pollution is the degradation of water quality by any process that changes ______.
e: Thermal pollution is the degradation of water quality by any process that changes ambient water temperature. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment. Oxygen concentration is not ambient water temperature.

q: Light pollution includes electronic billboards, night sports grounds, street lights, and ______.
e: Light pollution includes electronic billboards, night sports grounds, street lights, and residential areas. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment. Rivers is not residential areas.

q: Radioactive pollution is caused by the emission of high energy particles or radioactive substances from ______.
e: Radioactive pollution is caused by the emission of high energy particles or radioactive substances from nuclear weapons and nuclear fuel. Pollution is harmful extra material or energy put into the environment. Fossil fuels is not nuclear weapons and nuclear fuel.

q: A nutrient cycle is a repeated pathway of a particular nutrient from the physical environment to living organisms and back to the ______.
e: A nutrient cycle is a repeated pathway of a particular nutrient from the physical environment to living organisms and back to the environment. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic. Biological molecules occur naturally inside living organisms, not in bare rock. Atmosphere is different: the atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth.

q: The six main nutrient cycles include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorous, and ______.
e: The six main nutrient cycles include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorous, and sulphur. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule. Potassium is not sulphur.

q: Nitrogen gas constitutes ______ of the atmosphere.
e: Nitrogen gas constitutes 78% of the atmosphere. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule. 21% is not 78%.

q: The enzyme that catalyses the conversion of nitrogen gas into ammonia is called ______.
e: The enzyme that catalyses the conversion of nitrogen gas into ammonia is called nitrogenase. Nitrogenase is the enzyme that fixes nitrogen gas into a usable form. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule. Ammoniase is not nitrogenase.

q: Rhizobium forms a mutualistic association with the roots of ______.
e: Rhizobium forms a mutualistic association with the roots of legumes. Legumes host nitrogen-fixing Rhizobium in root nodules. Roots may use air spaces or aerenchyma when soil oxygen is low. Ferns is not legumes.

q: Ammonification is the process by which decomposers break down organic nitrogen to produce ______.
e: Ammonification is the process by which decomposers break down organic nitrogen to produce ammonia. Ammonification is microbes releasing ammonia from dead organic nitrogen. Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead material and recycle nutrients.

q: Nitrifying bacteria such as Nitrosomonas convert ammonium ions into ______.
e: Nitrifying bacteria such as Nitrosomonas convert ammonium ions into nitrites. Nitrites are the middle step as ammonia is oxidised toward nitrate. Nitrosomonas oxidises ammonia to nitrite in nitrification. Nitrates is not nitrites.

q: Denitrification converts nitrates into ______.
e: Denitrification converts nitrates into nitrogen gas. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule. Nitrites is different: nitrites are the middle step as ammonia is oxidised toward nitrate.

q: Phosphorus is a component of biological molecules such as RNA, DNA, phospholipids, and ______.
e: Phosphorus is a component of biological molecules such as RNA, DNA, phospholipids, and ATP. ATP is the cell's immediate energy currency. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides. Cellulose is different: cellulose is the beta-glucose polymer that makes plant cell walls rigid.

q: In the phosphorus cycle, phosphorus is released from rocks through the process of ______.
e: In the phosphorus cycle, phosphorus is released from rocks through the process of weathering. Weathering of rock releases mineral nutrients into soil. Rocks and soil belong to the lithosphere. Photosynthesis is different: photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light.

q: Sulphur is an essential component of many ______ and enzyme cofactors.
e: Sulphur is an essential component of many proteins and enzyme cofactors. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Carbohydrates is different: carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure.

q: When fossil fuels are burnt, sulphur is released as ______.
e: When fossil fuels are burnt, sulphur is released as sulphur dioxide (SO2). Sulphuric acid (H2SO4) is not sulphur dioxide (SO2).

q: A drug is any substance that is taken into the body that alters or influences ______ in the body.
e: A drug is any substance that is taken into the body that alters or influences chemical reactions in the body. Biochemistry looks at chemical substances and chemical processes in cells. Blood volume is not chemical reactions.

q: Penicillin is an antibiotic used to cure bacterial infections such as pneumonia, gonorrhoea, and ______.
e: Penicillin is an antibiotic used to cure bacterial infections such as pneumonia, gonorrhoea, and syphilis. Syphilis is a bacterial sexually transmitted infection. Penicillin is an antibiotic originally from a fungus. Influenza is not syphilis.

q: Aspirin is a sedative drug used as a ______.
e: Aspirin is a sedative drug used as a painkiller. Aspirin is a painkiller used as a medicine, an applied-biology product. Antibiotic is different: antibiotics kill or stop bacteria; they do not work on viruses.

q: Drug abuse refers to the use of chemicals for the purpose of creating ______ on the brain.
e: Drug abuse refers to the use of chemicals for the purpose of creating pleasurable effects on the brain. Memory loss is not pleasurable effects.

q: Heroin is a strong ______.
e: Heroin is a strong sedative. Heroin is a narcotic drug with strong withdrawal effects; it is not a biology tool. Stimulant is not sedative.

q: Withdrawal symptoms of heroin include insomnia, muscle cramps, sweating, headaches, diarrhoea, vomiting and ______.
e: Withdrawal symptoms of heroin include insomnia, muscle cramps, sweating, headaches, diarrhoea, vomiting and nausea. Heroin is a narcotic drug with strong withdrawal effects; it is not a biology tool. Fever is not nausea.

q: Excessive alcohol consumption can lead to stomach ulcers, heart disease, and ______.
e: Excessive alcohol consumption can lead to stomach ulcers, heart disease, and brain damage. Kidney stones is not brain damage.

q: Tobacco smoke contains harmful substances such as nicotine, tar, carbon monoxide and ______.
e: Tobacco smoke contains harmful substances such as nicotine, tar, carbon monoxide and smoke particles. Oxygen is different: oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration.

q: Smoking can lead to chronic bronchitis, emphysema, lung cancer, and increases the risk of ______.
e: Smoking can lead to chronic bronchitis, emphysema, lung cancer, and increases the risk of heart disease. Cancer is uncontrolled cell division after control checkpoints fail. Osteoporosis is not heart disease.

q: If a pregnant woman smokes, the baby may be born underweight or even ______.
e: If a pregnant woman smokes, the baby may be born underweight or even born dead. With deformities is not born dead.
